chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Amr ibn Yazeed, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I heard you saying: All of our Shias are in Paradise, in the state they were in.' He said, 'I have told you the truth. All of them, by Allah, are in Paradise.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, but sins are many and major.' He said, 'As for the Day of Resurrection, all of you will be in Paradise by the intercession of the Obeyed Prophet or the Successor of the Prophet. But, by Allah, I fear for you in the Barzakh.' I said, 'And what is the Barzakh?' He said, 'The grave, from the time of his death until the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.الْبَرْزَخ: The intermediate realm between death and resurrection, specifically referring to the grave period
key_terms.شَفَاعَة: Intercession, particularly by the Prophet and Imams

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the fate of Shia in the grave versus Paradise according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the ultimate salvation of the Shia in Paradise through the intercession of the Prophet and the Imams, and the intermediate state of the grave (Barzakh) where they may face trials or punishment for their sins. This hadith highlights the Shia theological concept of 'intercession' (Shafa'ah) as a guarantee of final entry into Paradise, while acknowledging the reality of post-mortem accountability in the Barzakh period. The narration underscores the importance of balancing hope in divine mercy with fear of one's deeds during the interval between death and resurrection.
